title: How LinkedIn, Netflix & DoorDash Run Agents, Evals & Inference in Production: QCon AI New York 2026
gist: Promotional program announcement for QCon AI New York 2026 (Dec 15–16) that nonetheless discloses concrete production-AI metrics from LinkedIn, Netflix, Figma, DoorDash, Harvey and Honeycomb on agent authorization, evals, inference scale and AI code review.

insights.claim: 1Password CTO Nancy Wang argues identity systems assume a human behind every credential, with a stable role, bounded session and post-hoc accountability, and that AI agents have none of these.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Agent identity/authorization is an emerging security product category; identity vendors are positioning for it.

insights.claim: Figma found the trust boundary for production agents extends beyond the sandbox; warm pools cut agent provisioning latency by 90% and raised availability from 99% to 99.95%.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Sandbox provisioning is a real operational cost center for agent platforms — opportunity for sandbox infra providers.

insights.claim: LinkedIn runs a Kubernetes operations agent across more than 500,000 nodes and 5 million pods, with guardrails enforced server-side via rate limits, delete protection and peer approval for production changes.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Large-scale SRE agents are in production; server-side guardrails, not prompt rules, are the control pattern.
insights.locator: Ronak Nathani, Principal Staff Software Engineer

insights.claim: DoorDash gates every change to its agentic ordering system with an LLM judge calibrated against human reviewers, using the same rubrics to score simulated and real sessions so offline gains carry into production.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Calibrated LLM-as-judge eval loops are becoming release gates, a demand driver for eval tooling.
insights.locator: Fabio Flores, Software Engineer at DoorDash

insights.claim: Netflix serves ML and generative AI from a single platform handling about 1 million inference requests per second across 300+ models after five years of consolidation.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Consolidated multi-tenant inference platforms at hyperscale imply sustained in-house GPU/serving demand.

insights.claim: Pinterest serves vision-language models on NVIDIA Dynamo for multimodal workloads with heavy prefill computation and large KV cache pressure.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: NVIDIA's software stack (Dynamo) is gaining production adoption in inference serving, extending its moat beyond hardware.

insights.claim: LinkedIn's AI code review system reviews tens of thousands of pull requests a week across about 10,000 repositories, with more than 60% of sampled suggestions accepted after a validation pipeline filters findings.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: High acceptance rates at scale validate AI code review as a durable enterprise use case.
insights.locator: Min Chen, Principal Staff Engineer at LinkedIn

insights.claim: Legal-AI firm Harvey shipped its agents internally first on its Spectre platform, which passed 7,000 merged pull requests across every repository before the agents reached lawyers.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Dogfooding agents on internal engineering is a common de-risking path before customer-facing launch.
insights.locator: Joey Wang, engineering lead at Harvey

insights.claim: Honeycomb's peak weekday PR merges to its main monorepo rose from about 30 to about 74 between early 2025 and April 2026 under its 2x initiative, and have held steady since.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: A ~2.5x throughput gain sustained over time is concrete evidence that AI coding productivity gains can persist.
insights.locator: Liz Fong-Jones, Technical Fellow at Honeycomb

insights.claim: OpenAI's Brian Yang frames the post-adoption problem: once every engineer has coding agents, one person's effective way of working is hard for teammates to reproduce.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Organizational diffusion, not tool access, may cap AI productivity gains — a market for agent-workflow standardization.
insights.locator: Brian Yang, Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI
